content: The test image shows a corn plant with what appears to be excessive tillering/multiple shoots from the base, somewhat stunted appearance, and light green/yellowish coloration. This suggests a systemic disease affecting whole plant growth. Top candidates: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma or Crazy_Top.

The reference image for Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows purple/brown sheath discoloration with black specks — this doesn't match the test image well.

Returning to the test image observations:
- Multiple shoots/tillers emerging from the base of the plant
- Plant appears stunted relative to healthy corn
- Leaves are somewhat narrow
- No obvious leaf lesions or spots visible
- Whole-plant systemic appearance

This pattern of excessive tillering and stunting points most strongly to **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**, which causes stunting, excessive tillering, and leaf discoloration. Crazy_Top would show more dramatic tassel/floral abnormalities. The multiple side shoots from the base are characteristic of spiroplasma infection.
